From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 31 Mar 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps: Trial criteria deep-dive & ops roadmap

Hi Elaine / Tom — thanks for the call today. Quick write-up of what we heard + a concrete proposal so we can lock the trial acceptance criteria and owners. Please review and confirm or flag any changes by EOD Fri.

Summary of goals (what Avery wants):
- Integrate Redwood inference to surface structured recommendations from your billing dataset; reduce manual review by ~60%.
- Keep end-user latency imperceptible.
- Validate quality against three canonical evaluation slices (Billing anomalies, Rate-plan mapping, Free-text normalization).

Proposed success criteria (trial pass/fail gates):
- Latency: p50 <= 120ms across 95% of requests; p95 <= 400ms for 95% of the test windows (measured at the API edge).
- Throughput: sustained 30 req/s for the canonical traffic profile (burst capacity to 100 req/s for 30s tolerated).
- Cost: average token cost <= $0.0009/token for the configured inference profile (includes batching and KV cache benefits).
- Quality: combined accuracy >= 92% on the three eval slices; hallucination/error rate <= 1.5% on the billing anomalies slice.
- Robustness: automatic fallback to smaller quantized variant if p95 exceeds 600ms for >3 consecutive minutes.

Evaluation plan & instrumentation:
- Redwood provides a perf harness (attached) and runbook: Ben will run baseline throughput/latency tests in a mirrored sandbox.
- Rishi will run the quality runs against Avery's golden labels (we request 1k examples per slice to start; later expand).
- Trial window: 6 weeks from kickoff. Week 0: sandbox integration + validation runs. Weeks 1–3: quality and perf iterations. Weeks 4–5: stability runs and tuning. Week 6: readout + decision.

Owners & immediate asks:
- Ben Carter (redwood) — perf harness, test schedule, and initial results by 2027-04-05.
- Rishi Malhotra (redwood) — eval scripts, scoring definitions, and first quality snapshot by 2027-04-08.
- Avery — sample labeling access (1k/sample slice), a test traffic profile export, and confirmation on retention/PII rules.

Attachments: avery_trial_matrix.xlsx (trial measurement matrix), redwood_kpi_definition.pdf (definitions and measurement methodology), perf-harness-instructions.md (how to run the sandbox harness).

Next steps (proposed):
1) Avery confirms sample delivery and retention constraints by Fri 2027-04-02.
2) Ben schedules perf run window for Apr 5–6 (we suggest 2-hour window).
3) Rishi to circulate scoring rubric and initial script by Apr 6.
4) Joint kickoff: Apr 7 — 30m alignment call to confirm instrumentation and access.

If this reads OK, please reply with confirmations and any additions to the success criteria.

Thanks — Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Thanks, Sergio — appreciate the clear breakdown. A couple quick clarifications before we lock: 

- Sample size: 1k per slice sounds fine for the initial quality signal, but for billing anomalies we might push to 2k to get stable estimates. We'll confirm thresholds after we upload.
- Perf environment: we prefer Redwood to run the initial perf harness from our staging cluster (VPC peered) so numbers reflect our network egress. Is that supported, or should we run an internal synthetic and share metrics?
- Cost measurement: do you include batching and expected tokenization differences caused by our preprocessor? We want the cost target to reflect realistic token counts.

We'll aim to deliver samples and a test traffic export by 2027-04-02; final confirmation from legal on retention rules is in progress (we'll update).

If Ben can propose a 2-hr window on Apr 5 in PST, we can lock it. Also happy to do the Apr 7 kickoff call — Tom and I will join.

—Elaine
Elaine Jones
Head of Data Products, Avery Systems

What we'll run in the window:
